children: By Bharath Rajeswaran and Vivek Kumar M

Indian shares edged lower on Tuesday, following the benchmarks' six-week low hit in the previous session, as sentiment remained subdued due to the widening Middle East conflict pushing crude prices higher.
The Nifty 50
lost 0.46% at 23,668.85 and the BSE Sensex
fell 0.53% to 75,727.30 as of 10:06 a.m. IST.

Any new attacks on Tehran will be met with retaliation on U.S. assets, Iran threatened on Monday, and warned that energy infrastructure across the Gulf, including U.S. oil and gas interests, was vulnerable.
Rising crude prices and renewed US–Iran hostilities are keeping risk appetite subdued, analysts said.
"Nifty could remain volatile around key support levels, while any recovery is likely to face selling at higher levels.  Hitesh Tailor, Technical Research Analyst at Choice Broking.
Brent crude futures
rose 0.6% to around $98 per barrel. India is particularly vulnerable to higher fuel prices as it imports about 85% of its crude requirements.
Twelve of the 16 major domestic sectors logged losses. Heavyweight financials
fell 0.7% and private banks (.NIFPVTBNK) slid 0.6%.
The three heaviest benchmark stocks, HDFC Bank
, ICICI Bank
and Reliance Industries
shed 0.7%, 1.1% and 0.6%, respectively.
The broader small-caps
and mid-caps
fell 0.3% each.
Among individual stocks, GE Vernova T&D India
climbed 8% after securing a high-voltage direct current contract from Power Grid
Temasek-backed Indian logistics firm Shiprocket
, which went public on August 19, gained 3.2% after its first-quarter loss narrowed.

"While the secondary market remains lacklustre, primary market continues to see strong action, with 12 IPOs opening this week, aiming to raise a combined 70 billion rupees in one of the busiest weeks of the current IPO cycle," said Siddhartha Khemka, head of research of wealth management at Motilal Oswal Financial.
State-owned Bharat Electronics
and Hindustan Aeronautics
added 2.3% and 3.7%, respectively, after India's defence acquisition council approved various proposals at an estimated cost of 1.1 trillion rupees.
